metaData.originalTitle: Faire doubles PR throughput with Cursor Cloud Agents · Cursor
metaData.title: Faire doubles PR throughput with Cursor Cloud Agents · Cursor
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Faire doubled its weekly PR throughput and collapsed an 18-month migration to a single engineer by using Cursor's cloud agents for scaled parallelization and autonomous task execution.
metaData.summary: This article details how Faire, an online marketplace, leveraged Cursor's cloud agents to dramatically increase its engineering velocity. By moving from local agent setups to Cursor's cloud infrastructure, Faire overcame resource constraints and achieved true parallelization. The key innovation is the use of cloud agents that each run in their own isolated development environment, allowing them to operate autonomously like human engineers. This enabled Faire to automate a massive legacy migration from MobX to React state management, reducing an 18-month team effort to a single engineer managing a fleet of agents. Beyond migrations, Faire uses Cursor Automations to run over 2,000 autonomous agent runs per week for tasks like triaging Slack bug reports, fixing CI failures, and routing code reviews. The article also highlights how a senior engineer used a cloud agent to build a full preview tool in less than a day, a task that would have taken weeks. The result is a 2-3x increase in engineering output, shifting the company's focus to scaling impact across adjacent teams.

mainPoints.point: Cloud-based AI agents enable true parallelization, overcoming local machine resource constraints.
mainPoints.explanation: Running multiple agents locally is limited by compute and management overhead. Cursor's cloud agents each get their own isolated environment, allowing for scaled, autonomous parallel task execution.

mainPoints.point: Cursor's cloud agents can automate complex, multi-step engineering tasks like legacy migrations.
mainPoints.explanation: Faire used a system called Swarm to coordinate Cursor agents for a MobX-to-React migration. A single engineer managed a fleet of agents, completing what was estimated as 18 months of manual work.

mainPoints.point: Programmatic agents (Cursor Automations) can handle repetitive tasks autonomously at scale.
mainPoints.explanation: Faire runs over 2,000 automated agent runs per week for tasks like triaging bugs from Slack, auto-healing CI failures, and routing PRs, saving significant manual labor.

keyQuotes: Cloud agents run without the memory and resource constraints of a local machine, and each one gets its own development environment---just like an engineer---to write code, test and verify its work, and ship software.
What would have been 18 months of manual work for a full team is now coordinated by a single engineer managing a fleet of cloud agents.
As teams get more leverage from coding agents, the constraints are shifting. The opportunity now is to help adjacent teams scale their impact as well.
